fitments.note: Dwelling with individual convenience: a bath room with a tap and floor trap, a water closet with flushing apparatus and ablution tap, a tap with floor trap or a sink in the kitchen or wash place.

amenities.note: At least one water closet, one lavatory, one kitchen sink and one bathing place.

population.note: Residential population: 1 bedroom 4, 2 bedroom 5, 3 bedroom 6, 4 bedroom and above 7.

overhead_tank.note: Only an OHT provided: 33.33 to 50 percent of one day's requirement; the upper bound is used.

subcircuit.note: Light/fan/6 A socket sub-circuit: at most ten points and 800 W; power sub-circuit: at most two 16 A outlets.

lighting_density.note: Lighting demand at most 13 W/m2 of built-up area; power at least 55 W/m2 with diversity not over 50 percent.

two_pipe.note: Two-pipe system: soil stack for water closets, waste stack for sinks and washing; stacks on the external wall face. Pipe routing is LOD 300 and not modelled.

points.note: Points per room: no NBC count; typical Indian residential practice.

heights.note: Mounting heights above finished floor: switch boards 1.2 m, 6 A sockets 0.3 m (kitchen 1.1 m), TV 0.45 m, AC 16 A 2.1 m, geyser 16 A 1.8 m, washing machine 16 A 1.0 m.

socket_height.note: Ordinary socket-outlet at a height above 200 mm from the floor level.

accessible.note: For persons with disabilities and the elderly: switches and socket-outlets between 800 and 1 100 mm above floor level, at least 600 mm (preferably 700 mm) from any internal corner. Written for public buildings; applied here because the household includes elderly or wheelchair users.

loads.note: Connected load per point: LED light 20 W, fan 60 W, 6 A socket 100 W, 16 A outlet 1000 W.

stack_clearance.note: Stacks kept 75 mm clear of column faces for pipe clamps and access, 40 mm of beam faces (beams are flush with the wall; practice; NBC Part 9 Section 2 asks that stacks be accessible but gives no figure).
